headline: High: Goose’s shared-filesystem, shell, and broad-network defaults create dangerous interaction risks with Firecrawl’s web-extraction and API-key handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API scraping surfaces, so malicious page text can reach Goose through shared workflows. Goose can use MCP and reads/writes the filesystem, making it plausible it will treat Firecrawl output as actionable content. The bridge is indirect, but default interaction exists.
conditions: IF Goose consumes Firecrawl scrape/map output as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF Firecrawl is pointed at attacker-controlled pages and Goose processes the resulting text, prompt injection can propagate.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all Firecrawl outputs before Goose reads them.
Require Goose to treat Firecrawl output as untrusted data only.
Restrict Firecrawl targets to allowlisted domains.
Insert a manual review step before any Goose tool action.
requires-engineering: add structured output schemas and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl handles API keys and broad network egress, while Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and can run shell/MCP tools. If they share a workspace, Goose can expose files or secrets that Firecrawl then transmits to third-party endpoints. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path in default-style use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or cwd, Goose can read files Firecrawl later sends out.
IF API keys or screenshots are present in shared files, Firecrawl may transmit them over its network egress.
mitigations: Separate Firecrawl and Goose workspaces.
Store secrets outside any shared directory.
Disable Firecrawl access to sensitive folders.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Firecrawl supports multiple instances and also touches files via its API/CLI/MCP client pattern. On a shared directory, concurrent writes or git mutations can collide, and the profiles do not show locking or coordination. Uncertainty about orchestration increases, so the higher severity is chosen.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF Goose modifies git state while Firecrawl writes generated artifacts, repository corruption or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees or branches per agent.
Check in-progress files before each write.
requires-engineering: add file locks or an orchestrator-level mutex.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces extracted web content and structured data that Goose can consume through MCP/filesystem workflows. Goose has shell and git authority, so if it treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, downstream actions can be wrong or unsafe. The pair is not fully autonomous, but the default dataflow supports error propagation.
conditions: IF Goose uses Firecrawl output without verification, incorrect facts can be acted on.
IF Firecrawl extracts stale or adversarial web content, Goose may propagate those errors into shell or git actions.
mitigations: Require Goose to verify extracted facts against a second source.
Mark Firecrawl output as untrusted by default.
Limit Goose actions to dry-run mode for first pass.
Review diffs before git commits.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and citation checks before actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content and API keys, while Goose handles source code and local files with broad filesystem access. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through Firecrawl’s external API use and Goose’s local file handling. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so this is a general compliance risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, Goose can retain it locally while Firecrawl sends related content externally.
IF organizational policy forbids external processing of web content or secrets, Firecrawl’s egress can violate it.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Use separate retention policies for each agent.
Disable Firecrawl on sensitive projects.
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls.
